Standard: Air vehicles flying above 10,000 feet MSL are capable of providing emergency oxygen from the air vehicle, or from a stand-alone system, to each passenger until the air vehicle is able to descend below 10,000 feet. The passenger emergency oxygen system, such as automatic dispensing units and portable oxygen generation packs, will be in compliance with 14 CFR 25.1441, 25.1443, 25.1445, 25.1447, and 25.1449. The supply of oxygen is sufficient for the duration of time that passengers may be exposed to cabin altitudes up to 40,000 feet while breathing up to 30 liters per minute, Body Temperature Pressure Saturated, and with a tidal volume of 1.1 liters. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review drawings or digital mockups to verify emergency oxygen provisions. a. Ensure that the total number of portable emergency oxygen generators or dispensing units in passenger sections exceeds the number of seats by at least 10%. b. Ensure that at least two oxygen dispensing units are connected to oxygen terminals in each lavatory.
(2) Inspect air vehicle and oxygen system specifications to ensure all operational phases are accounted for in the altitude protection system hardware.
(3) Review FMECA to verify that all emergency oxygen systems are covered. Analysis.
  (1) Verify Oxygen System Safety Analysis shows that failures across the system are annunciated and have automatic responses.
  (2) Conduct analyses to determine the life limits for components within the emergency oxygen system based upon reliability and durability data.
  (3) Conduct review of materials, connectors, wiring, and subsystem assemblies to ensure compatibility with the air vehicle. Demonstration.
    (1) Using a mockup or production air vehicle, demonstrate that passengers are able to access the emergency oxygen system and don them within five seconds at each location.
    (2) On air vehicle with automatic dispensers, demonstrate that the units are deployed before the cabin pressure altitude exceeds 15,000 feet.
